title: Student loan forgiveness available for NYS nursing educators, young farmers - Newsday
text:

 NYS offering student loan forgiveness for nursing educators, young farmers
 Gov. Kathy Hochul announced student loan forgiveness is now available for NYS nursing educators, young farmers. Credit: AP/Yuki Iwamura
 By Darwin Yanes darwin.yanes@newsday.com Updated November 20, 2026 4:30 pm Share Applications for two state loan forgiveness programs aimed at providing relief to nursing educators and young farmers are open through Dec. 16, Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Friday.
 Eligible applicants can have student loans forgiven by up to $40,000 for nursing faculty and $50,000 for farmers. The nursing program is open to applicants eligible for the 2025 program year, while the farmers program is open for the 2026 program year.
 "From the nurses who train our future healthcare professionals to the farmers who help feed our families, New York depends on people who dedicate their careers to serving others," Hochul said in a news release. "Student debt shouldn’t stand in the way of their careers, and that’s what these loan forgiveness programs are all about."
 recommended New: Newsday's Essential Guide to College in NY The requirements to qualify for the nursing loan forgiveness program  include: An applicant must be a registered nurse professionally licensed to practice in New York, possess a master’s degree in nursing or a doctoral degree qualifying them to serve as nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty and must have clinical experience as a licensed registered nurse.
 Applicants must be nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty at a nursing school in the state, and teach at least 12 credit hours annually.

 To qualify for the Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program , applicants must have earned an undergraduate degree from an approved New York State college or university, be within their first 10 years of operating a farm in the state that produces agricultural products and operate the farm on a full-time basis.
 The programs are administered by the New York State Higher Education Services Corporation and officials said combined, the loan programs have $2.1 million available to assist students in these fields with their debt.
 "These programs help New Yorkers pursue meaningful careers in two fields that are essential to our state’s future," New York State Higher Education Services Corporation acting president Doris B. González said in a statement.
 By Darwin Yanes darwin.yanes@newsday.com Darwin Yanes is a native Long Islander and Stony Brook University graduate who covers education. He previously covered the Town of North Hempstead.
